topic.name: NVIDIA NICo (NVIDIA Infra Controller)
topic.goal: Understand, deploy and operate NVIDIA NICo well enough to provision bare-metal machines through its APIs.

concepts.name: Admin CLI
concepts.definition: A command-line tool for site administrators that connects directly to the API Service over mTLS/gRPC. It is used, for example, to set site-wide credentials.

concepts.name: API Service (NICo Core)
concepts.definition: NICo's central control-plane service and single source of truth. It is the only service that reads and writes PostgreSQL, it implements state machines for managed resources, and other services talk to it over mTLS/gRPC.

concepts.name: Bare-metal lifecycle management
concepts.definition: Managing physical servers from the moment they are racked: discovery, validation, provisioning to tenants, ongoing operation, and cleanup for reuse. The goal is for physical machines to behave like cloud instances.

concepts.name: Baseboard Management Controller (BMC)
concepts.definition: A small, independent controller on a server or DPU that allows remote power control, monitoring and firmware updates over a management network, even when the main OS is down.

concepts.name: BGP
concepts.definition: The routing protocol networks use to exchange routes. In NICo each DPU runs eBGP, often unnumbered (peering over link-local IPv6), with leaf switches or route servers to advertise its loopback and tenant routes.

concepts.name: BlueField DPU
concepts.definition: An NVIDIA SmartNIC with its own ARM CPU, OS and BMC. It sits in the server and handles networking independently of the host. In NICo it is the trust anchor and the point where network isolation is enforced.

concepts.name: cert-manager
concepts.definition: A Kubernetes controller that issues and rotates TLS certificates from configured issuers, such as the site-root CA or Vault PKI. NICo uses it for its mTLS certificates.

concepts.name: cloud-init
concepts.definition: A standard tool for configuring an OS on first boot from supplied user-data. NICo's PXE Service serves cloud-init user-data to hosts.

concepts.name: DHCP
concepts.definition: The protocol devices use to get IP addresses automatically. A DHCP relay forwards requests from one network segment to a central server. NICo discovers BMCs when their relayed DHCP requests reach nico-dhcp.

concepts.name: DNS (authoritative and recursive)
concepts.definition: An authoritative DNS server answers for zones it owns. A recursive resolver looks up any name for clients. NICo runs both: an authoritative server for its delegated zones, and unbound for managed machines.

concepts.name: DPU Agent
concepts.definition: A persistent daemon on the DPU's ARM OS. Every 30 seconds it asks the API Service for the desired network configuration, applies it through HBN, and reports back the state it observes. It also handles health checks and updates.

concepts.name: DPU mode vs NIC mode
concepts.definition: A BlueField can run in DPU mode, where its ARM OS manages networking, or in NIC mode, where it acts as a plain NIC. Hosts in NIC mode and hosts without a DPU (zero-DPU hosts) use central DHCP on HostInband instead of a local DHCP server on the DPU.

concepts.name: External Secrets Operator (ESO)
concepts.definition: A Kubernetes operator that copies secrets from a backing store into Kubernetes Secret objects. In NICo it copies CA bundles and DB credentials into NICo namespaces.

concepts.name: GitOps with ArgoCD
concepts.definition: Continuous delivery where a controller syncs cluster state from Git. It is an optional way to deploy and update NICo.

concepts.name: Hardware Health service
concepts.definition: A NICo service that scrapes host and DPU BMCs over Redfish for sensor data and firmware inventory. It exposes /metrics and /telemetry and reports health alerts to the API Service.

concepts.name: HashiCorp Vault
concepts.definition: A secrets manager whose PKI engine issues certificates and whose KV engine stores credentials. NICo services authenticate to it with Kubernetes auth. It is optional: the --skip-vault install keeps credentials in Postgres instead.

concepts.name: Host-Based Networking (HBN)
concepts.definition: NVIDIA's networking stack that runs Cumulus Linux routing in containers on the DPU, configured through NVUE. NICo uses it to enforce VXLAN/EVPN tenant isolation without changing the physical switches.

concepts.name: Kubernetes
concepts.definition: A container orchestration platform. NICo's control plane is deployed on it as microservices and needs v1.30 or later.

concepts.name: Managed Host
concepts.definition: A host server paired with one or more BlueField DPUs that NICo manages. The DPUs act as the enforcement boundary for network isolation and security.

concepts.name: Metadata Service (FMDS)
concepts.definition: A service on the DPU that gives tenant workloads instance metadata, such as machine ID and boot info, through a local HTTP API on the host-facing interface.

concepts.name: MetalLB LoadBalancer VIPs
concepts.definition: MetalLB gives bare-metal Kubernetes LoadBalancer services virtual IPs and advertises them over BGP or L2. This makes NICo pods reachable from BMCs, the admin network and tenant VPCs.

concepts.name: mTLS / gRPC
aliases: TLS certificate chain and root CA
concepts.definition: gRPC is a binary RPC protocol. Mutual TLS means both client and server present certificates to prove their identity. All NICo control-plane services talk to each other using gRPC over mTLS.

concepts.name: Network planes (Ethernet, InfiniBand, NVLink)
concepts.definition: The separate fabrics in an AI cluster. Ethernet carries north-south traffic, InfiniBand and Spectrum-X carry east-west GPU traffic, and NVLink connects GPUs. NICo isolates tenants on each of them.

concepts.name: NICo (NVIDIA Infra Controller)
concepts.definition: An open source suite of microservices for site-local, zero-trust lifecycle management of bare-metal hosts. It handles discovery, firmware, DPU provisioning, network isolation and tenant sanitization, and exposes all of this through APIs.

concepts.name: NICo REST (JSON API)
concepts.definition: The REST API that exposes NICo to operators and ISVs, authenticated with JWT. It can be deployed next to the site controller or centrally in the cloud, serving multiple sites.

concepts.name: NICo scope boundaries
concepts.definition: NICo covers everything from the physical underlay up to the OS boot handoff. OS management, cluster assembly (Kubernetes/SLURM), workload scheduling and switch configuration belong to the platform or network team.

concepts.name: Observability stack (Prometheus, Grafana, Loki, OpenTelemetry)
concepts.definition: Tools for metrics scraping (Prometheus), dashboards (Grafana), log aggregation (Loki) and telemetry shipping (OpenTelemetry Collector). NICo exports Prometheus metrics and sends logs to Loki.

concepts.name: OIDC / JWT authentication (Keycloak)
concepts.definition: OIDC is a standard for logging in through an identity provider such as Keycloak, which issues signed JWT tokens. NICo REST accepts JWTs, and the admin web UI uses OIDC.

concepts.name: PKI and TLS certificates
aliases: Public key infrastructure and CA trust
concepts.definition: Public key infrastructure: a certificate authority signs certificates that bind identities (DNS names in the SANs) to keys. Services use these certificates for TLS and mTLS.

concepts.name: PostgreSQL (Zalando operator)
concepts.definition: The relational database holding all NICo state. Only the API Service reads and writes it. The reference deployment uses the Zalando Postgres Operator and needs the btree_gin and pg_trgm extensions.

concepts.name: PXE / iPXE boot
concepts.definition: Booting a machine over the network, where firmware fetches boot scripts and OS images from a server. NICo's PXE Service delivers iPXE scripts, cloud-init data and images over HTTP.

concepts.name: Redfish API
concepts.definition: A standard REST/HTTPS API exposed by BMCs for out-of-band management: power control, boot order, firmware inventory and update, sensors, and Serial-over-LAN. NICo talks to BMCs only through Redfish.

concepts.name: Scout
concepts.definition: A temporary agent that runs on the x86 host during discovery. It collects hardware inventory that cannot be gathered out-of-band, runs validation tests, and reports to the API Service.

concepts.name: Serial-over-LAN and SSH Console Service
concepts.definition: Serial-over-LAN carries a server's serial console over the BMC network. NICo's SSH Console Service keeps SSH/IPMI connections to BMCs open so admins and tenants get live console access, and the output is logged to Loki.

concepts.name: Site Agent
concepts.definition: A site-controller service that keeps a Temporal connection to NICo REST. It syncs data and passes requests on to the local API Service, so NICo REST can run centrally while sites run on-premises.

concepts.name: Site Controller
concepts.definition: The NICo control plane: a suite of microservices running on a Kubernetes cluster of at least three nodes, located in the datacenter it manages.

concepts.name: State machine (resource lifecycle)
concepts.definition: A model where each managed resource, such as a host or network segment, moves through defined states (for example Decommissioning/Decommissioned) with controlled transitions between them.

concepts.name: Temporal workflow engine
concepts.definition: A durable workflow orchestration engine. NICo REST uses it for multi-step operations such as provisioning and release, and the Site Agent connects through it. It needs the cloud and site namespaces plus one per site UUID.

concepts.name: UEFI firmware and Secure Boot
concepts.definition: UEFI is the server firmware that initializes hardware and picks the boot device. Secure Boot only allows signed bootloaders and kernels to run. NICo manages UEFI settings, boot order and passwords.

concepts.name: Zero-trust host model
concepts.definition: NICo's principle that software inside the host OS is never trusted for security or isolation decisions. Enforcement happens on the DPU, and monitoring happens out-of-band.

concepts.name: Firmware baseline enforcement
concepts.definition: Taking inventory of UEFI/BMC firmware and updating hosts to a site-defined baseline. Hosts that cannot be brought to the baseline are quarantined. Later updates are scheduled on healthy, unoccupied hosts.

concepts.name: GB200 NVL72 rack-scale management (NICo Flow)
concepts.definition: NICo's rack-level management for GB200 NVL72 systems. It treats racks and NVL domains as units and sequences power, firmware, leak response and power profiles across the trays in a rack.

concepts.name: Hardware discovery and ingestion
concepts.definition: NICo's zero-touch Day 0 process. It finds BMCs over the OOB network, collects inventory through Redfish, pairs DPUs to hosts using LLDP and serial numbers, and brings hosts under management.

concepts.name: InfiniBand partitioning with UFM (P_Key)
concepts.definition: InfiniBand isolates traffic with partition keys (P_Keys). NVIDIA's UFM fabric manager assigns them, and NICo calls UFM APIs to put a tenant's ports into that tenant's partition.

concepts.name: LLDP
concepts.definition: A layer-2 protocol where devices advertise their identity to directly connected neighbors. NICo uses it to work out which DPU belongs to which host.

concepts.name: Multi-tenancy
concepts.definition: Several customers (tenants) share the same physical infrastructure, and each must be isolated from the others.

concepts.name: NVLink partitioning with NMX-C
concepts.definition: NMX-C is the NVLink fabric controller. NICo uses its gRPC API to place GPUs into tenant NVLink logical partitions and to check that the NVLink domain is healthy before allocating instances.

concepts.name: Out-of-band (OOB) management
concepts.definition: Managing and monitoring hardware over a separate management network through BMCs, without going through the host OS. NICo relies only on out-of-band paths so a compromised host cannot spoof or block monitoring.

concepts.name: Secure Erase
concepts.definition: A drive-level command that cryptographically or physically wipes all data on NVMe/SAS/SATA drives. NICo requires drives that support it.

concepts.name: Site-wide BMC and UEFI credentials
concepts.definition: Site-managed passwords that NICo sets on host/DPU BMCs and UEFI after it takes over from the factory defaults. They must be configured before ingestion starts.

concepts.name: SKU validation and burn-in
concepts.definition: Checking that each machine has the expected hardware components for its SKU, then running hardware and connectivity tests (including NVLink and InfiniBand multi-node tests) before the host is made available.

concepts.name: Tenant sanitization
concepts.definition: The cleanup after a tenant releases a host. It includes secure disk erase, memory-overwrite verification, IB reset, TPM clear, re-attestation, and network cleanup that only counts as complete once the DPU confirms it has left all tenant networks.

concepts.name: TPM and Measured Boot attestation
concepts.definition: A TPM chip records hashes of boot components in Platform Configuration Registers (PCRs). Attestation checks these measurements and the TPM's signature, using the TPM Manufacturer CA, to prove a host booted untampered. In NICo it is off by default.

concepts.name: UEFI lockdown
concepts.definition: Locking UEFI/BIOS settings while a tenant has the host, together with disabling in-band host-to-BMC access, so the tenant cannot change firmware configuration.

concepts.name: VPC (FNN VPC)
concepts.definition: A tenant's isolated virtual network, set up through the API. In FNN VPCs each instance interface gets a routed /31 link to its DPU gateway, and there is no shared L2 subnet.

concepts.name: VRF
concepts.definition: A separate routing table on one device, which keeps each tenant's routes isolated from the others.

concepts.name: VXLAN / EVPN
concepts.definition: VXLAN wraps Layer-2/3 traffic in UDP so overlay networks can run over a routed underlay. EVPN is the BGP address family that spreads overlay reachability. DPUs act as the VXLAN tunnel endpoints (VTEPs).

concepts.name: Static network fabric principle
concepts.definition: Leaf/spine switches are never reconfigured when tenants change. All tenant isolation is done on DPUs and through fabric manager APIs.

concepts.name: Day 0 / Day 1 / Day 2 lifecycle
concepts.definition: NICo's three lifecycle phases. Day 0 covers bring-up, discovery and ingestion. Day 1 covers isolation, lockdown and provisioning. Day 2 covers operations, monitoring, upgrades and tenant transitions.

concepts.name: Instance and instance type
concepts.definition: An instance is a host allocated to a tenant. An instance type is an operator-defined hardware class used to request hosts through the API.

concepts.name: IP address pools
concepts.definition: Address ranges the site owner gives NICo for allocation: OOB management, DPU loopbacks, admin network, tenant networks (/31 per interface), and control-plane service VIPs.

concepts.name: Underlay and overlay networks
concepts.definition: The underlay is the physical routed network of switches. Overlays are virtual networks tunneled over it, such as tenant VPCs or the admin network.

concepts.name: VNI (L2VNI / L3VNI)
concepts.definition: The ID that tells VXLAN overlay segments apart. Each VPC needs a unique L3VNI for its VRF, and the admin network uses one L2VNI. VNIs must be unique across the datacenter.

concepts.name: CNI
concepts.definition: The Kubernetes plugin layer that provides pod networking. Calico is validated for NICo. Tenant clusters need a CNI that works over routed (not L2) node connectivity.

concepts.name: PF and VF (SR-IOV)
aliases: UEFI boot order and BIOS settings
concepts.definition: SR-IOV lets one NIC appear as a physical function (PF) plus several lightweight virtual functions (VFs). NICo gives each PF or VF its own tenant interface and /31.

concepts.name: Autonomous System Number (ASN)
concepts.definition: An identifier for a BGP routing domain. NICo gives every DPU a unique 32-bit ASN from a pool, following RFC 7938 data-center routing practice.

concepts.name: CIDR prefixes and /31 point-to-point subnets
concepts.definition: CIDR notation gives the size of an IP block. A /31 holds exactly two addresses for a point-to-point link, and a /32 is a single host address such as a loopback.

concepts.name: Route targets (import/export)
concepts.definition: BGP EVPN tags attached to routes that decide which VRFs import them. NICo uses conventional values (:50100 to :50500) so tenant/admin networks and control-plane VIPs can reach each other.

concepts.name: Kubernetes Custom Resource (CR/CRD)
concepts.definition: A user-defined Kubernetes API object type. Operators reconcile these objects into real state. DPF exposes CRs such as DPUDeployment, DPUFlavor and BFB.

concepts.name: Expected Machines Manifest
concepts.definition: A JSON file listing each host's BMC MAC address, chassis serial number and factory BMC credentials. Only hosts in this file are discovered and ingested.

concepts.name: API admission control
concepts.definition: A nico-api setting, on by default, that limits how many requests run and wait in a queue, both in total and per client. Disable it for simulated fleets, because all simulated agents share one client identity. Keep it on with real hardware and watch the rejection counter.

concepts.name: BMC network IP addressing
concepts.definition: Planning the address ranges for BMCs. Every endpoint needs one IP, and a 1,112-rack site needs 78,952 addresses, more than one /16 subnet (65,536) holds.

concepts.name: Calico networking
concepts.definition: A Kubernetes network plugin. Its calico-node pod runs the BIRD BGP daemon, whose health probes needed longer timeouts once nodes carried very many addresses.

concepts.name: Client identity
concepts.definition: The identity, typically from the client's certificate, that nico-api uses to apply per-client limits. On real hardware each host and DPU agent has its own identity.

concepts.name: DOCA Platform Framework (DPF)
concepts.definition: NVIDIA's framework for provisioning and orchestrating services on DPUs. NICo provisions DPUs through it, and scale tests use a DPF simulator in its place.

concepts.name: Fleet-up and time to ready
concepts.definition: The clock used for the simulation figures. It starts once every simulator pod is Ready and every simulated BMC is reachable, and it measures how long until all machines are created and every device reaches 'ready'.

concepts.name: GB200 NVL72 rack
concepts.definition: An NVIDIA rack-scale system made of 18 compute trays (hosts), 9 NVLink switch trays and several power shelves. Its GPUs share a single NVLink domain.

concepts.name: Helm chart values
concepts.definition: Configuration files that customize a Helm deployment. NICo ships sizing values, for example for 10k and 20k hosts, through them.

concepts.name: kube-proxy IPVS mode
concepts.definition: A kube-proxy mode that routes Service traffic with Linux IP Virtual Server. Each node keeps one ipset of addresses that holds at most 65,536 entries, which caps a stock simulator at about 736 racks.

concepts.name: Kubelet working set and OOM kill
concepts.definition: The working set is resident memory plus active page cache. It naturally grows toward the memory limit, so the real sign that more memory is needed is a rising oom_kill count in the container's cgroup.

concepts.name: Kubernetes resource limits
concepts.definition: Per-container caps on CPU and memory set in the pod spec or Helm values. Kubernetes reports CPU in logical CPUs (hyper-threads).

concepts.name: Kubernetes Service externalIP
concepts.definition: A Kubernetes Service field that exposes a Service on a specific IP address. The simulator publishes each simulated BMC address this way.

concepts.name: Machine-a-tron
concepts.definition: NICo's fleet simulator. It runs simulated BMCs and agents in Kubernetes pods behind a protocol gateway so the control plane can be scale-tested without real hardware.

concepts.name: Network security group
concepts.definition: A set of tenant firewall rules that the DPU agent enforces. A group is limited to 200 expanded rules by default.

concepts.name: NVLink switch tray
concepts.definition: A rack tray holding NVLink switches that connect the GPUs in an NVL72 rack. It runs NVOS and has its own BMC.

concepts.name: Pod anti-affinity
concepts.definition: A Kubernetes scheduling rule that keeps certain pods off the same node. The 20k-host runs used it to put nico-api and the Postgres primary on different nodes.

concepts.name: Power shelf
concepts.definition: A rack component that supplies power to the trays. It has a BMC and NICo manages it as a device that moves through to the ready state.

concepts.name: Prometheus metrics
concepts.definition: Time-series counters and histograms that components expose for monitoring. The sizing figures and alert signals come from them.

concepts.name: Rack Management Service (RMS)
concepts.definition: The service NICo uses for rack-level setup. Simulations use a mock of it.

concepts.name: Rack profile
concepts.definition: Configuration in the nico-api chart that says how many compute trays, DPUs, switch trays and power shelves a rack type has. NICo uses it to work out BMC endpoints and machines per rack, for example 71 endpoints and 54 machines for a GB200 NVL72 rack with 2 DPUs per tray.

concepts.name: Scale guidance vs hard limit
concepts.definition: NICo has no enforced maximum on fleet size. The published figures are the largest fleets measured, each labelled with how it was validated: field deployment, hardware lab, simulation, pre-release simulation, planned certification or roadmap.

concepts.name: State controller concurrency
concepts.definition: The machine state controller moves at most max_concurrency machines through their states at once (10 by default, 80 to 120 recommended for large sites). This setting, not the number of CPU cores, sets how long a fleet takes to become ready.

concepts.name: Tokio worker threads
concepts.definition: The threads that run the async Rust Tokio runtime inside nico-api. Raise their count to match nico-api's CPU limit so the extra CPU actually gets used.

concepts.name: VNI resource pool
concepts.definition: Operator-configured ranges of VNIs that NICo hands out to VPCs. The size of the pool bounds how many VPCs a site can have, and an established pool can be extended with nico-admin-cli.

concepts.name: VXLAN and VNI
concepts.definition: VXLAN carries layer-2 overlay networks over a routed fabric. Each overlay is identified by a VNI, and VTEPs are the endpoints of the tunnels.

concepts.name: Boot artifacts
concepts.definition: The OS images and binaries that NICo serves to network-boot hosts and DPUs. They are built with mkosi and iPXE and packaged into containers.

concepts.name: Build host bootstrap (make bootstrap)
concepts.definition: A single, repeatable step on Ubuntu 24.04 that installs the packages, rustup, git submodules, Docker with emulation, and cargo tooling needed for the full image and boot-artifact builds.

concepts.name: Building all images (make images)
concepts.definition: Make targets that build and push the deployable stack (NICo Core and the REST images), and optionally the machine-validation and boot-artifact images, for chosen architectures. A loop afterwards checks each tag's platforms.

concepts.name: Building local dev images (make images-dev)
concepts.definition: Builds one native Core development service image, such as api or dhcp, using the same recipes as Tilt, in a Linux Docker daemon. It does not push or deploy the image.

concepts.name: Container registry
concepts.definition: A server that stores and serves container images. The Makefile pushes to a local registry on localhost:5000 unless you override IMAGE_REGISTRY.

concepts.name: Cross-architecture emulation (binfmt/QEMU)
concepts.definition: Linux binfmt_misc registration with QEMU, which lets a host build and run images for a different CPU architecture. The -arm build targets avoid it by building natively.

concepts.name: Docker BuildKit and Buildx
concepts.definition: BuildKit is Docker's image build engine and Buildx is its CLI front end. NICo's build recipes pin both the Docker context and the builder so that every build runs on one daemon.

concepts.name: DPU BFB
concepts.definition: The BlueField Bootstream image format used to install software on a DPU. NICo builds it as the aarch64 boot artifact.

concepts.name: Multi-architecture image manifest
concepts.definition: A single image tag that points to separate images for each CPU architecture. NICo builds amd64 and arm64 separately and then assembles the combined tag.

concepts.name: nico-dhcp and Kea hook
aliases: Kea DHCP server with NICo hook
concepts.definition: NICo's central DHCP service, built as a Kea DHCP server hook. It is a stateless proxy that turns DHCP requests into gRPC discover_dhcp calls to Core, which assigns the IP addresses.

concepts.name: Rust toolchain and Cargo
concepts.definition: Rust's compiler and package/build tool. NICo is written in Rust, and its build tasks are driven with cargo-make.

concepts.name: Tilt
concepts.definition: A local Kubernetes development tool that builds and deploys services when code changes. NICo's dev image recipes are shared with it.

concepts.name: Admin and underlay networks
concepts.definition: Networks NICo creates at startup. The admin network carries host management traffic. Underlay data-plane networks are defined one per L3 segment. An IPv4 prefix needs a gateway.

concepts.name: Credential store (Vault vs Postgres)
concepts.definition: Where NICo keeps BMC and UEFI credentials. It is Vault by default, or PostgreSQL when the site is installed without Vault. In the Postgres case, certificates come from the site-issuer ClusterIssuer instead.

concepts.name: Helm and helmfile
concepts.definition: Helm is the Kubernetes package manager. It installs charts configured through YAML values files. helmfile declaratively manages several Helm releases and uses the helm-diff plugin to show what will change.

concepts.name: KMIP KEK provider
concepts.definition: An opt-in feature that gets the key-encryption keys protecting stored secrets from an external KMIP key-management server. The connection uses client TLS files (ca.pem, client.pem, client.key).

concepts.name: Kubernetes Ingress and ingress controllers
concepts.definition: An Ingress routes external HTTP(S) traffic to Services by hostname, and an ingress controller such as Contour/Envoy or nginx handles it. You can use one to expose nico-rest-api on a domain name with TLS instead of a NodePort.

concepts.name: Kubernetes Service types (LoadBalancer, NodePort, ClusterIP)
concepts.definition: The ways a Kubernetes Service can be exposed. ClusterIP is reachable only inside the cluster. NodePort opens a port on every node. LoadBalancer gets an external IP, which MetalLB supplies on bare metal.

concepts.name: Kubernetes workload and config objects
concepts.definition: The basic Kubernetes resources the docs refer to constantly. Pods run containers. StatefulSets run replicated stateful apps. Secrets and ConfigMaps hold credentials and configuration. Jobs run one-off tasks. Services expose pods on the network.

concepts.name: Kustomize
concepts.definition: A Kubernetes tool that customizes manifests by layering overlays on top of base manifests. setup.sh can apply a site overlay with it, and the REST stack uses kustomize bases.

concepts.name: Layer 2 advertisement (ARP)
concepts.definition: A MetalLB mode for flat networks without BGP. A node answers ARP requests for the VIP on the local network segment.

concepts.name: NICo resource pools
concepts.definition: Ranges that NICo allocates from. They cover loopback IPs for hosts and DPUs, VLAN IDs and VXLAN VNIs. All three must be non-empty.

concepts.name: nicocli
concepts.definition: The CLI for the NICo REST API, built from rest-api/. It is used for site management, org bootstrap and instance operations.

concepts.name: NTP time synchronization
concepts.definition: A protocol for keeping clocks synchronized. NICo uses enterprise NTP servers to set BMC time before ingestion. It can also run a 3-replica chrony service (nico-ntp) whose addresses are handed to DPUs over DHCP.

concepts.name: OAuth2 client credentials flow and JWT bearer tokens
concepts.definition: A machine-to-machine flow in which a client exchanges its ID and secret for a signed JWT access token, then sends it in an Authorization: Bearer header. The token's iss claim must match what the API expects.

concepts.name: Org bootstrap (InfrastructureProvider, Tenant, TenantAccount)
concepts.definition: A one-time GET call to the REST API. It lazily creates the org's InfrastructureProvider, a Tenant, and a TenantAccount linking them. Site operations return 404 until it has been called.

concepts.name: Out-of-band (OOB) management network
concepts.definition: A separate management network that connects the BMCs. Its switches must relay BMC DHCP requests to the nico-dhcp VIP so that NICo can find the hosts.

concepts.name: Persistent storage (StorageClass, PVC, local-path-provisioner)
concepts.definition: The Kubernetes system for durable volumes. local-path-provisioner creates StorageClasses backed by node-local disks, and the PostgreSQL and Vault volume claims use them.

concepts.name: Preflight checks (preflight.sh)
concepts.definition: A validation script that runs at the start of setup.sh. It checks environment variables, required tools, MetalLB config, cluster reachability, node count, kernel parameters, DNS, registry connectivity and Vault-free values. Errors stop the setup.

concepts.name: setup.sh orchestrator
concepts.definition: The script in helm-prereqs/ that installs every prerequisite and NICo component in numbered phases (0 to 7i). Flags such as --skip-vault, --skip-dpf and -y control it. It is idempotent, so you upgrade by re-running it.

concepts.name: Site and site UUID registration
concepts.definition: Each NICo installation manages exactly one site, which has a stable UUID. setup.sh reuses, adopts or mints the UUID and registers the site automatically, so you must not create sites manually.

concepts.name: siteConfig (site TOML configuration)
concepts.definition: A TOML block in nico-core.yaml that defines the site's identity, DHCP and NTP servers, fabric prefixes, deny prefixes, resource pools and initial networks.

concepts.name: TLS certificates and X.509 SAN
concepts.definition: Certificates that prove a server's identity and enable encrypted connections. Subject Alternative Names list the hostnames a certificate covers, and a wildcard covers exactly one DNS label.

concepts.name: Upgrade and teardown
concepts.definition: To upgrade, re-run setup.sh with new image tags; it preserves Vault, Postgres, MetalLB config and the site UUID. clean.sh removes all NICo components, namespaces and released volumes.

concepts.name: Virtual IP address (VIP)
concepts.definition: A stable IP address assigned to a service rather than to one machine. Each NICo Core LoadBalancer service needs a fixed VIP from the MetalLB pool so that DHCP relays, DNS and PXE can be configured in advance.

concepts.name: VLAN
concepts.definition: A virtual LAN, which splits one physical Layer 2 network into isolated segments identified by a VLAN ID. NICo allocates VLAN IDs from a configured pool.

concepts.name: bf.cfg parameters
concepts.definition: Install-time shell variables that the BFB installer sources, for example a hashed password for the DPU's ubuntu user. NICo appends them verbatim to the flavor.

concepts.name: BMC credential rotation
concepts.definition: Moving managed BMCs to a new versioned password. DPF v26.4.0 does not support this, so rotation must not be staged while DPF manages any DPU.

concepts.name: cert-manager approver-policy
concepts.definition: An optional cert-manager component that approves a certificate request only if a matching CertificateRequestPolicy allows it. Without a policy for dpf-operator-system, DPF's certificate requests stay Pending.

concepts.name: containerd
concepts.definition: The container runtime on each DPU that pulls and runs DPUService images.

concepts.name: Credential source modes (local / local_first / backend)
concepts.definition: Settings that decide where NICo reads the BMC root from: a locally mounted file or environment variable, or a persistent backend such as Vault or Postgres. In local mode, version 0 must exist before Core starts.

concepts.name: DPF maintenance hold (NodeEffect)
concepts.definition: A DPF phase where a DPU waits behind a maintenance hold before a disruptive change is applied. The DPU keeps serving traffic while it waits.

concepts.name: DPFOperatorConfig
concepts.definition: The operator-level DPF custom resource. For NICo it disables DPU auto-detection, turns on Redfish-based install, and sets the API server VIP and port, the Argo CD namespace, the MTU and the pull secrets.

concepts.name: DPU agent bootstrap CA
concepts.definition: The policy for how the DPU agent gets the root CA it uses to trust the NICo API: by the legacy download or from a mounted Secret or ConfigMap. Includes a procedure for rotating the root using an overlap bundle.

concepts.name: DPU reprovisioning
concepts.definition: Reinstalling a DPU's OS. This happens when its flavor or BFB changes, or when an operator triggers it, for example after enabling DPF on an existing host.

concepts.name: DPUCluster
concepts.definition: The DPF custom resource that defines the Kubernetes control plane DPU nodes join. Here it is Kamaji-based and reached through a keepalived VIP.

concepts.name: DPUDeployment
concepts.definition: The DPF custom resource that ties together a BFB or BlueField software, a flavor and service templates for one DPU generation. NICo creates one per active deployment: BF3 always, and BF4 generic or BF4 Astra when configured.

concepts.name: DPUFlavor / DPUFlavorTemplate
concepts.definition: The DPF custom resource that describes a DPU's OS configuration, such as bf.cfg parameters and the proxy drop-in. Its name includes a hash of its spec, so any change creates a new flavor and triggers DPU reprovisioning. Astra uses a Go-template variant.

concepts.name: DPUService CR set (Interface/Template/Configuration/NAD)
concepts.definition: The DPF custom resources that carbide-api creates for each mandatory service. Together they define the service's chart, its configuration, its network interfaces and its network attachment.

concepts.name: DPUService rollout gating
concepts.definition: NICo marks DPUService updates as disruptive, so each DPU is held in DPF's NodeEffect phase until it matches its DPUDeployment. The hold is then released automatically for idle Ready hosts, or by an operator with dpf service-sync release.

concepts.name: HTTPS/SOCKS5 forward proxy for DPU egress
concepts.definition: An optional proxy that DPUs route image pulls through. NICo puts it into a containerd systemd drop-in inside the DPUFlavor, so changing it triggers reprovisioning.

concepts.name: IPv6 metadata transport
concepts.definition: An optional setup that serves FMDS metadata over IPv6. It needs overlays on both the DPU agent chart (to select the HBN peer) and the FMDS chart (for the listener and address).

concepts.name: iPXE-based DPU provisioning
concepts.definition: The older, now deprecated NICo way of provisioning DPUs, where they network-boot with iPXE. A host stays on this path when dpf_enabled = false.

concepts.name: Jumbo frames / MTU
concepts.definition: The maximum packet size on a link. 9000-byte jumbo frames are used on the high-speed fabric.

concepts.name: Kamaji
concepts.definition: A tool that runs Kubernetes control planes as pods inside a host cluster. DPF uses it to host the DPU cluster's control plane.

concepts.name: Kubernetes RBAC
concepts.definition: Kubernetes' role-based access control. Roles list the allowed verbs on resources, and bindings grant those roles to identities such as ServiceAccounts.

concepts.name: Kubernetes Secret
concepts.definition: A Kubernetes object that holds sensitive data such as passwords or registry credentials. Pods can reference it, for example to pull private images.

concepts.name: Managed Host Lifecycle
concepts.definition: The main sequence of top-level states a managed host goes through: DPU discovery, DPU initialization, host initialization, Ready, Assigned to an instance, and cleanup. There are side paths for validation, reprovisioning, measuring, failure and decommissioning.

concepts.name: Node Feature Discovery (NFD)
concepts.definition: A Kubernetes add-on that labels nodes based on their hardware features. With NICo, nodes are labelled through NFD's own config (PCI class 0200) instead of the NodeFeatureRules bundled with the DPF chart.

concepts.name: Scalable Functions (SF)
concepts.definition: Lightweight virtual network functions carved from a DPU's physical function. NICo reserves SFs for HBN service-VPC interfaces and for extra capacity.

concepts.name: Selectorless Service with manual Endpoints
concepts.definition: A Kubernetes pattern: if a Service has no selector and an Endpoints object exists with the same name, Kubernetes uses those endpoints exactly as written. Here a dummy IP is used so the Service routes nothing.

concepts.name: Site-wide BMC root credential
concepts.definition: The shared BMC password that NICo applies to managed hardware. carbide-api copies its current version into the bmc-shared-password Secret every 60 seconds so DPF can reach BMCs. DPU registration is blocked until this credential is set.

concepts.name: Tenant instance
concepts.definition: A tenant workload allocated to a host. Releasing a hold on a host with an instance disrupts that tenant, so the operator must name the instance explicitly.

concepts.name: TOML
concepts.definition: A configuration file format built from tables and key-value pairs. NICo's site config is written in it.

concepts.name: AES-GCM symmetric encryption
concepts.definition: An authenticated symmetric cipher that uses a shared secret key (here 256-bit) to provide both confidentiality and integrity. Additional authenticated data (AAD) binds extra context into the ciphertext.

concepts.name: Envelope encryption and KEK
concepts.definition: Data is encrypted with data keys, and those keys are in turn encrypted (wrapped) with a master key encryption key (KEK). You keep the KEK safe and track its key ID so you can rotate it.

concepts.name: Machine identity (JWT-SVID issuance)
concepts.definition: A NICo feature that signs short-lived SPIFFE JWT-SVIDs for workloads on instances, through the Core gRPC API or IMDS. Each org has its own signing keys, which are encrypted under the site KEK.

concepts.name: Rate limiting (GCRA token bucket)
concepts.definition: An algorithm that caps the sustained request rate and allows short bursts. The DPU agent uses it for IMDS identity requests.

concepts.name: SPIFFE
concepts.definition: A standard for workload identity. Workloads get a SPIFFE ID within a trust domain and prove it with an SVID, which is either an X.509 certificate or a JWT.

concepts.name: Token delegation (RFC 8693 token exchange)
concepts.definition: An OAuth standard for exchanging one token for another at a security token service (STS). NICo can use it to delegate tokens to external STS endpoints, optionally through an egress proxy.

concepts.name: Factory default credentials
concepts.definition: The vendor default BMC and UEFI passwords that NICo needs to log into new hardware for the first time. They can be seeded into Vault, imported, or added through the CLI.

concepts.name: Desired vs actual state reconciliation
concepts.definition: A control pattern where requests record what should be true and background loops keep acting until the real system matches it.

concepts.name: DPU-host pairing
concepts.definition: Site Explorer works out which DPU belongs to which host by matching the serial numbers reported by host and DPU BMCs, then checks DPU mode and completeness.

concepts.name: Loki logging
concepts.definition: A log aggregation system queried through Grafana or logcli. It stores logs from control-plane components and host serial consoles.

concepts.name: Machine Update Manager
concepts.definition: A Core scheduler that picks hosts and DPUs with outdated firmware for automatic updates. The ManagedHost state machine then carries out the updates.

concepts.name: Preingestion Manager
concepts.definition: A Core module that updates firmware, runs resets and recovers DPU BFB images on hosts that are too old to be ingested normally.

concepts.name: Underlay and HostInband network segments
concepts.definition: NICo's physical network segment types. Underlay carries BMC and DPU out-of-band interfaces. HostInband is shared by zero-DPU host OS interfaces and, optionally, their BMCs.

concepts.name: Component Manager
concepts.definition: A pluggable layer that performs hardware operations for one class of component (compute tray, switch, power shelf) through a configured backend such as RMS or direct Redfish.

concepts.name: Asynchronous job polling
concepts.definition: A pattern where a request returns a job ID right away, and the caller polls a status API until the job reaches completed or failed.

concepts.name: Power control reset types
concepts.definition: The Redfish reset actions used to power-cycle hosts and DPUs. They range from a graceful restart to a full AC power cycle.

concepts.name: libredfish and nv-redfish
concepts.definition: The two Rust Redfish client libraries NICo uses. libredfish has vendor-specific implementations. nv-redfish generates typed code from the Redfish schema and is gradually replacing libredfish.

concepts.name: BMC sensors and event logs
concepts.definition: Redfish endpoints that report temperatures, fan speeds, power readings and BMC/system event log entries. NICo polls them periodically, and fetches logs incrementally.

concepts.name: Boot order and boot source override
concepts.definition: The list of devices a server tries to boot from, plus a one-time or persistent override set through Redfish. NICo uses it to make hosts boot from the network.

concepts.name: Firmware inventory and update
concepts.definition: The Redfish UpdateService lists firmware components and their versions and accepts firmware updates. NICo compares these versions with its configuration to decide on upgrades.

concepts.name: MAC address
concepts.definition: The hardware address of a network interface. NICo uses MACs to identify interfaces and BMCs, to pair DPUs with hosts, and as the key for storing BMC credentials.

concepts.name: Machine ID
concepts.definition: NICo's stable identifier for a machine. It is generated by hashing DMI data such as the system serial number and manufacturer, so a missing serial number breaks identification.

concepts.name: PCIe device
concepts.definition: A hardware component attached over the PCI Express bus, such as a NIC, DPU or GPU. Redfish exposes PCIe devices with serial and part numbers, and NICo uses them as the primary path for DPU pairing.

concepts.name: Redfish resource tree (Systems, Chassis, Managers)
concepts.definition: Redfish arranges resources in a hierarchy under /redfish/v1. Systems are the computers, Chassis are the physical enclosures and cards, and Managers are the BMCs. Resources link to each other with @odata.id references.

concepts.name: Redfish Task Service
concepts.definition: Redfish resources that track long-running asynchronous operations, such as firmware updates, so a client can poll for completion.

concepts.name: Redfish vendor detection and OEM extensions
concepts.definition: NICo reads the Vendor field from the service root and uses it to choose vendor-specific endpoints and behavior (Dell, HPE, Supermicro, Lenovo, Viking, NVIDIA). Vendors also add non-standard fields and actions under an 'Oem' section.

concepts.name: rshim
concepts.definition: A BlueField interface that lets the host (or the BMC) reach the DPU's console and boot path over PCIe. NICo enables it with NVIDIA OEM Redfish actions.

concepts.name: SKU validation
concepts.definition: A check that a host's discovered hardware (CPU, memory, GPUs, IB NICs) matches its expected SKU definition. A failure raises a SkuValidation alert.

concepts.name: SPDM attestation
concepts.definition: A protocol for checking a hardware component's identity and firmware measurements using certificates and signed measurements. NICo triggers evidence collection through Redfish ComponentIntegrity and has its own controller for it.

concepts.name: UEFI device path
concepts.definition: A UEFI string that describes the hardware path to a device, e.g. PciRoot(...)/Pci(...)/MAC(...). NICo parses it to order interfaces and to extract MAC addresses.

concepts.name: UEFI/BIOS settings
concepts.definition: Firmware configuration of a server. Redfish lets clients read BIOS attributes and write them as pending changes that take effect on the next reboot. NICo uses this for things like enabling SR-IOV.

concepts.name: Database transaction
concepts.definition: A group of database writes that commit or roll back together. NICo keeps transactions short and never holds one open across external calls.

concepts.name: Idempotency
concepts.definition: An operation is idempotent if repeating it gives the same result as doing it once. NICo requires handlers and external effects to be safe to retry, because exactly-once execution is not guaranteed.

concepts.name: Iteration invalidation
concepts.definition: When a conditional state write is rejected, the processor rolls back all writes from that iteration and immediately requeues the resource to reload fresh state. This is not recorded as an error.

concepts.name: Optimistic concurrency / stale-write protection
concepts.definition: Writing state only if its stored version still matches the version that was read. NICo rejects stale writes this way and invalidates that iteration.

concepts.name: Recovery point and crash-window reconciliation
concepts.definition: Before an external call, persist enough durable state to resume or reconcile it after a crash. Afterwards, classify the result as absent, complete, partial/unwanted or unknown, and act safely, failing closed when unsure.

concepts.name: Service-level agreement (SLA) for states
concepts.definition: A time limit for how long a resource should stay in a given lifecycle state. When it is exceeded, the framework records an SLA error that deployments can alert on.

concepts.name: State controller work queue and claims
concepts.definition: Resources are queued periodically, after transitions, or on explicit request. A processor then claims them in the database and handles them with bounded concurrency and a timeout. Another processor can reclaim a claim that has gone stale.

concepts.name: State handler outcomes
concepts.definition: What a handler returns from one pass. Wait and DoNothing keep the state. Transition stores the next state and requeues. Deleted removes the queue claim.

concepts.name: WorkLock lease and fencing
concepts.definition: An expiring, auto-renewed database lease for coordinating long-running work. Protected writes must call fence_transaction in the same transaction to prove the worker still owns the lease.

concepts.name: Admin network isolation
concepts.definition: An internal NICo setting that overrides the tenant's network configuration and places the machine on an isolated admin network. This is used during provisioning and termination.

concepts.name: Force delete of managed host
concepts.definition: Removing a host without the normal deprovisioning states. Extra logic is then needed to detach it from external fabric partitions.

concepts.name: Health alert classifications
concepts.definition: Tags on a health alert that say how NICo reacts. For example, PreventAllocations stops tenants from receiving the host. Decisions check these tags instead of specific alert IDs.

concepts.name: Machine capabilities and instance types
concepts.definition: Capabilities are computed from hardware discovery and describe a machine's configurable interfaces, such as IB ports and GPUs. Instance types list the capabilities tenants can rely on, and must be a subset of the machine's capabilities.

concepts.name: Aggregated host health
concepts.definition: nico-core merges the health reports from all sources into one host health. It uses this for allocation and state-transition decisions, shows it to admins, and shows a filtered version to tenants.

concepts.name: Health report overrides (Merge/Replace)
concepts.definition: An API that lets admins or external tools add health reports. Merge adds alerts alongside NICo's own, while Replace ignores built-in alerts and uses only the override.

concepts.name: HealthReport
concepts.definition: NICo's data structure for health information. It records a source, a timestamp, and lists of successful and failed probes, each identified by a probe id and optional target. It is built to be merged across sources.

concepts.name: Machine validation tests
concepts.definition: Admin-defined shell-script tests that scout runs on a host at ingestion, after cleanup, or on demand. A failure places a health alert that blocks allocation.

concepts.name: Alert debouncing
concepts.definition: Raising an alert only after a set number of consecutive failed checks, and clearing it on the first success, so short blips are not reported.

concepts.name: BMC sensor thresholds
concepts.definition: Ranges that a sensor reports: caution, critical, fatal and valid min/max. nico-hardware-health maps them to the SensorWarning, SensorCritical, SensorFatal and SensorFailure classifications.

concepts.name: Building Management System (BMS)
concepts.definition: Datacenter facility systems. NICo receives their rack leak events through the DSX Exchange consumer.

concepts.name: DPU restricted mode
concepts.definition: A locked-down DPU mode in which the host cannot reconfigure the DPU. NICo raises an alert if the DPU is not running in it.

concepts.name: Health probe ID
concepts.definition: A stable identifier for one specific health check, for example BmcSensor or HeartbeatTimeout, used to label alerts and successes in health reports.

concepts.name: InfiniBand GUID and LID
concepts.definition: A GUID is the globally unique hardware ID of an InfiniBand port or VF. A LID is the local address that the subnet manager assigns.

concepts.name: Leak detection
concepts.definition: Health processing that turns raw leak observations (from BMC detectors, NVUE switch sensors or the BMS) into derived tray-level and rack-level leak alerts.

concepts.name: Maintenance mode
concepts.definition: An admin marking that a host is being worked on. It applies PreventAllocations, SuppressExternalAlerting and ExcludeFromStateMachineSla.

concepts.name: NMX-T
concepts.definition: The NVLink telemetry listener service that runs on primary switches.

concepts.name: NVLink isolation
concepts.definition: Removing all of a host's GPUs from every NVLink partition, triggered by the IsolateFromNvLinkPartitions classification. It is used before a compute tray is moved or replaced.

concepts.name: NVLink partition monitor
concepts.definition: A periodic nico-api task that reconciles NVLink partitions with NMX-C. It raises NmxcUnreachable and NvlinkUnhealthy alerts and performs isolation.

concepts.name: NVOS / NVUE
concepts.definition: The NVIDIA switch and network operating system (NVOS) and its configuration and state API (NVUE). They are used on switches and in HBN on DPUs.

concepts.name: Repair workflow
concepts.definition: A flow in which tenants report broken hosts on release, or flag instances for online repair, so an external framework can fix them.

concepts.name: Switch reachability monitor
concepts.definition: A nico-api task that makes a TCP connection to each ready switch's NVOS and NMX-T ports, and raises debounced unreachable alerts.

concepts.name: Targeted instance creation
concepts.definition: Creating an instance on a specific Machine ID. In some cases this can bypass health-based allocation blocks.

concepts.name: Top-of-rack (ToR) uplink
concepts.definition: The DPU's physical uplink ports (p0 and p1) to the rack switches. Normal PXE boot requires p0.

concepts.name: SuppressExternalAlerting
concepts.definition: A classification that leaves a host out of the site-wide fleet-health calculation, so known issues do not trigger external alerts.

concepts.name: Key group
concepts.definition: A named set of SSH public keys, stored per tenant, that grants access to the SSH console.

concepts.name: Key group synchronization
concepts.definition: The process in which the cloud REST API pushes versioned key group contents to sites, records which version each site holds, and compares versions to find out of sync sites.

concepts.name: SSH public keys
concepts.definition: Public keys that authorize a user to log in over SSH. Here they grant access to the host's serial console.

concepts.name: Device-instance to hardware mapping
concepts.definition: The rule that turns a tenant's (device, fabric, device_instance) selection into a specific hardware port: matching devices are sorted by PCI slot and the N-th is chosen.

concepts.name: Discovery data
concepts.definition: The hardware details that nico-scout reports and NICo stores in its database, including InfiniBand devices with PCI properties and GUIDs.

concepts.name: InfiniBand device (NIC port as device)
concepts.definition: A physical PCI function that can send InfiniBand traffic. NICo presents each port of a multi-port NIC as a separate device.

concepts.name: InfiniBand fabric
concepts.definition: A separate InfiniBand network. Each NIC port connects to one fabric, and a host may span several fabrics.

concepts.name: InstanceInfinibandConfig
concepts.definition: The tenant's InfiniBand configuration for an instance. Each interface selects a device by name, fabric and device_instance, chooses a PF or VF, and names a partition.

concepts.name: Mellanox firmware tools (mlxconfig, mst)
concepts.definition: Command-line tools for inspecting and configuring ConnectX NIC firmware settings, such as link type and the number of VFs. They operate per physical card.

concepts.name: NUMA node
concepts.definition: A CPU and memory locality domain. The NUMA node a device is attached to affects performance between that device and GPUs.

concepts.name: PCI device and slot address
concepts.definition: An address such as 0000:ca:00.0 that identifies a PCI device. NICo sorts by it to map tenant selections to hardware deterministically.

concepts.name: Protocol Buffers
concepts.definition: A schema language and serialization format that NICo uses to define API messages such as InfinibandInterface.

concepts.name: BGP Peering with Top-of-Rack Switch
concepts.definition: The DPU's BGP session to the rack's switch on its uplink port (p0). A p0 transport failure blocks the PXE restart.

concepts.name: BOSS Controller
concepts.definition: A Dell boot-drive controller. NICo securely erases it and recreates its volume during cleanup.

concepts.name: Decommissioning
concepts.definition: The terminal path from Ready. It resets host and DPU configuration, suppresses DHCP for the host's MACs, factory-resets the BMCs, and deletes per-device credentials.

concepts.name: Disable Onboard NICs (Vera Rubin)
concepts.definition: A HostInit step only for Vera Rubin hosts with managed DPUs. It enables and then disables the onboard NICs through the BMC, with persisted 10-second waits between the writes.

concepts.name: DMI Platform Identity
concepts.definition: The system vendor and product name that the host firmware reports. NIC firmware policy uses them to identify the platform.

concepts.name: DPA (Data Path Accelerator)
concepts.definition: A NIC subsystem with its own agents and firmware policies. Legacy DPA firmware paths must not overlap with the generic NIC firmware engine.

concepts.name: Failed State and Failure Causes
concepts.definition: A state recording why a host failed, such as BIOS setup, discovery, measurement or validation failures. Some causes recover automatically once the condition clears, others need an admin.

concepts.name: Firmware Supervisor and Receipt
concepts.definition: The local daemon that performs firmware work, plus the receipt Core saves that records which work it accepted and the results. Core uses receipts to resume after restarts without repeating writes.

concepts.name: Host Reprovision
concepts.definition: Updating host firmware through the BMC, either by uploading images or by running scripts, followed by a reset and verification. It can run from Ready or Assigned.

concepts.name: Live Network Update
concepts.definition: Changing an assigned instance's networking without restarting the host. NICo keeps the old resources until every DPU acknowledges the new configuration and health is clear, then releases them in one transaction.

concepts.name: Managed Artifact Cache
concepts.definition: Storage for firmware artifacts. Admitted operations pin their artifacts by digest so they are not evicted during use.

concepts.name: Managed-Host Reset
concepts.definition: An admin-requested reset that deletes the instance and re-ingests the host. It is the supported way to recover a parked NIC firmware failure.

concepts.name: Managed-Machine Update Scheduling Budget
concepts.definition: A shared limit on how many hosts can do firmware updates at once. If both limits are unset, capacity is zero and changed NIC work stays pending.

concepts.name: Network Configuration Version Acknowledgement
concepts.definition: DPU agents report which version of the desired network configuration they have applied. NICo waits until the reported versions match the desired versions before moving on.

concepts.name: NIC Firmware Baseline Policy
concepts.definition: The target firmware chosen per card, machine or site, in that order of precedence. A change only proceeds if the platform (sys_vendor/product_name) and the card (PN/PSID) exactly match the allow-list.

concepts.name: NIC Firmware Execution Phases
concepts.definition: The steps an admitted operation goes through for each card: observe the supervisor, unlock, flash, then activate by reboot or card reset. It then checks a fresh inventory and restores the original lockdown policies.

concepts.name: NIC Firmware Recovery Engine
concepts.definition: An unreleased, disabled-by-default part of the state machine. It checks non-DPU NIC firmware against a baseline during initial preparation and deprovision, and admits and tracks firmware changes so they can be recovered safely.

concepts.name: NIC Readiness Qualification and Restoration Obligations
concepts.definition: Persisted flags saying a NIC card must be restored to baseline or re-qualified through host preparation before allocation. They survive reset and admission being disabled.

concepts.name: Operator Reconciliation
concepts.definition: The manual procedure used when evidence is uncertain. The operator fences all original senders, preserves the evidence, confirms that tools and hardware have settled, and then conditionally records settlement for the exact token.

concepts.name: Out-of-Band (OOB) Interface
concepts.definition: A management network interface that is separate from the data network.

concepts.name: PN/PSID
concepts.definition: The part number and Parameter-Set ID that identify an NVIDIA NIC model and its firmware configuration. They are used to match cards to the allow-list.

concepts.name: State History and Manual Intervention Alerts
concepts.definition: Diagnostic tools for stuck hosts. State history shows past transitions and errors, and alerts fire when the controller needs an operator to step in.

concepts.name: SuperNIC Lockdown
concepts.definition: A card mode that blocks firmware and configuration changes unless the card is unlocked with a 64-bit key, so host tenants cannot tamper with the NIC. Losing the key effectively bricks the card.

concepts.name: Tracked Dispatch
concepts.definition: A record (UUID token and origin) that each participating sender writes before sending a power, DPA or MLX command. An unresolved dispatch blocks further progress until the command's effects are proven settled.

concepts.name: BOM Validation
concepts.definition: A switch state that checks the switch against its expected Bill of Materials (the list of components it should have).

concepts.name: NMX-C / Fabric Manager
concepts.definition: The NVLink fabric management cluster application that runs on the primary switch. The rack's ConfigureNmxCluster step rotates switch certificates, then submits an RMS ScaleUpFabricManager V2 job that picks the primary switch and binds NMX-C.

concepts.name: On-Demand Maintenance
concepts.definition: A maintenance operation requested by an operator, such as PowerOn, PowerOff, Reset or ReconfigureCertificate. It is stored as a request on the device record. The state controller picks it up, runs it, and clears the request when done.

concepts.name: Switch Certificate Configuration
concepts.definition: The Configuring sub-flow that first disables any existing mTLS bindings (DisableMtls) and then installs NVOS certificates (ConfigureCertificate) through asynchronous RMS jobs. Maintenance can rerun the installation step as ReconfigureCertificate.

concepts.name: Switch ReProvisioning
concepts.definition: A rack-driven switch state. The switch waits in turn for the rack firmware upgrade, the NVOS upgrade and NMX-C configuration, while the rack updates status fields on the switch.

concepts.name: Switch State Machine
concepts.definition: The lifecycle of an NVLink switch in NICo. It runs Created → Initializing → Configuring → FetchInfo → Validating → BomValidating → Ready. From Ready the switch can enter Maintenance, ReProvisioning, Decommissioning, Error or Deleting.

concepts.name: Controller State Persistence
concepts.definition: Each device's current state and sub-state are stored as JSON in a PostgreSQL column, such as switches.controller_state. This lets a restarted controller continue where it left off.

concepts.name: NVLink scale-up fabric
concepts.definition: The NVLink network that links GPUs across trays in a rack into one larger GPU domain. The fabric manager and telemetry services manage and monitor it.

concepts.name: Primary Switch
concepts.definition: The one switch in a rack that RMS selects to host the fabric manager and telemetry cluster applications. Certificate requests for those services only target this switch.

concepts.name: Submission Outcome Semantics
concepts.definition: Error categories that say whether RMS might have received a request. RejectedBeforeDispatch is safe to retry. OperationOutcomeUnknown goes to Error rather than risk running a non-idempotent operation twice. Unsupported means the step is skipped.

concepts.name: Switch mTLS Services
concepts.definition: A configurable list of switch services (nvue_api and the scale-up fabric telemetry, manager and telemetry interface services) that get certificate bindings. Fabric services apply only to the primary switch.

concepts.name: Power Shelf State Machine
concepts.definition: The lifecycle of a power shelf in NICo. It runs Initializing → FetchingData → Configuring → Ready. Operators can trigger on-demand PowerOn/PowerOff maintenance, and the shelf can also be decommissioned or deleted.

concepts.name: PowerSequence Reboot Barrier
concepts.definition: A rack maintenance step that queues graceful reboots for a saved batch of compute hosts. It waits until each host reports a reboot timestamp newer than the time the batch was saved.

concepts.name: Rack Ingestion
concepts.definition: The automatic first maintenance cycle a newly discovered rack goes through. It upgrades firmware on ready devices and admits hosts that arrive late into the same firmware job. A real NVOS update during this cycle triggers a compute reboot.

concepts.name: Rack Maintenance
concepts.definition: The rack state in which NICo runs maintenance activities in order: FirmwareUpgrade, NVOSUpdate, an optional PowerSequence reboot barrier, and ConfigureNmxCluster, then Completed. Some activities can be skipped depending on the maintenance scope.

concepts.name: Rack State Machine
concepts.definition: The lifecycle of a rack, which is a collection of compute trays, switches and power shelves: Created → Discovering → Maintenance → Validating → Ready. It coordinates and drives the state machines of its child devices.

concepts.name: Rack Validation (RVS)
concepts.definition: Rack validation run by the RVS service. RVS writes run-id and partition result labels on the rack's machines, and those labels move the rack's Validating sub-states forward until the rack is Validated or Failed.

concepts.name: Tray Replacement / Topology Change
concepts.definition: An external event where a compute tray is physically replaced. The old machine is deleted, a new one is discovered, and the rack goes back from Ready to Discovering.

concepts.name: Maintenance Activities
concepts.definition: The steps a maintenance run can include: firmware upgrade, NVOS update, power sequence and NMX cluster configuration. They always run in that fixed order. An empty list selects everything except the power sequence.

concepts.name: Maintenance Scope
concepts.definition: The optional lists of machine, switch and power-shelf IDs to maintain. If all three lists are empty, the whole rack is maintained.

concepts.name: On-Demand Rack Maintenance
concepts.definition: A gRPC operation that sets a maintenance request on a rack in Ready or Error. The rack state machine then picks it up, runs the selected maintenance activities, and returns the rack through Validating to Ready.

concepts.name: Role-Based Access Control (RBAC)
concepts.definition: Granting permissions to roles instead of individual users. For example, Core grants OnDemandRackMaintenance to the NicoAdminCLI role, and REST uses provider/tenant admin and viewer roles.

concepts.name: SOT JSON
concepts.definition: A JSON document that defines the target firmware or system-image configuration and is passed to RMS. It comes either from the rack profile's firmware object or from an explicit maintenance activity.

concepts.name: State Controller Tick
concepts.definition: The periodic loop in which a state handler reloads an object from the database, checks its config flags, and performs any transition. A gRPC call only sets a flag; the actual transition happens on a later tick.

concepts.name: DPA Interface
concepts.definition: NICo's record and lifecycle for a SuperNIC attached to a host. It moves through Unlocking, firmware/profile application, Locking and Assigned.

concepts.name: Entropy and Offline Guessing
concepts.definition: A secret's strength comes from how unpredictable it is. HKDF adds no entropy, so if a card key leaks, a weak IKM could be guessed offline.

concepts.name: HKDF-SHA256
concepts.definition: The standard HMAC-based KDF from RFC 5869. NICo applies it with no salt and an info string of `supernic-lock:v1:{mac}:{machine_id}` to produce each card's 8-byte lockdown key.

concepts.name: Input Key Material (IKM)
concepts.definition: The secret, high-entropy, site-wide value that all lockdown keys are derived from. It is versioned and kept in the credential store, and the key cannot be re-derived without the exact version used.

concepts.name: KDF Context
concepts.definition: The non-secret inputs that tie a derived key to one card: its MAC address and the owning host's MachineId, encoded in the versioned V1 format.

concepts.name: Key Derivation Function (KDF)
concepts.definition: A function that deterministically produces cryptographic keys from secret input material plus context. The same inputs always give the same key, and different contexts give independent keys.

concepts.name: Lockdown IKM Rotation
concepts.definition: Creating a new IKM version and moving cards to it. Cards migrate at allocation or through idle unlock/re-lock, and the version chosen depends on in-flight, current and site-target bookkeeping.

concepts.name: S-VPC
concepts.definition: A non-ASTRA deployment flavour (for example on BF3) where SuperNICs are flashed so that NICo must manage their lockdown keys.

concepts.name: BMC Discovery
concepts.definition: How NICo finds BMCs. A BMC requests an IP address over DHCP (relayed to NICo), and NICo matches its MAC address against the expected-machines table to look up its initial credentials.

concepts.name: DOCA
concepts.definition: NVIDIA's software framework and release train for BlueField DPU functionality.

concepts.name: EVPN
concepts.definition: A BGP-based control plane that tells VTEPs which tenant addresses are reachable where in a VXLAN overlay.

concepts.name: Flat VPC
concepts.definition: A VPC type for zero-DPU hosts. NICo allocates addresses and keeps records, but the operator's fabric does the routing and enforcement.

concepts.name: Host DPU Policy
concepts.definition: The operator's chosen treatment of DPU hardware on a host. `Manage` lets NICo provision the DPUs, `Nic` runs them as plain NICs, and `Ignore` leaves them unconfigured. It records intent, not what the hardware is actually doing.

concepts.name: HostInband Network Segment
concepts.definition: An underlay segment that a zero-DPU host's NIC attaches to directly. It is the only segment type a Flat VPC accepts.

concepts.name: Mellanox Device Kind
concepts.definition: The factory product class NICo derives from a card's part number. It identifies the SKU and does not change when the card's operating mode changes.

concepts.name: Asynchronous programming (async/await)
concepts.definition: A programming style where tasks pause while waiting for I/O, so a small number of threads can run many tasks.
